title: Finite column sample intersection
statement: Let $X,Y\subseteq\mathbb{R}$ be nonempty sets, with $X$ compact and convex and $Y$ convex. Suppose $f:\mathbb{R}\times\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ is continuous and convex in its first variable on $X$ for each $y\in Y$, concave in its second variable on $Y$ for each $x\in X$, bounded above and below on $X\times Y$, and satisfies $0\le f(x,y)\le1$ for all $x\in X$ and $y\in Y$. For an integer $M>1$, a sample $x_1,\ldots,x_M\in X$, a real number $\varepsilon>0$, and a finite set $v\subseteq Y$, define $K=\sup_{y\in Y}\inf_{1\le i\le M}f(x_i,y)$. There is a point $x'\in X$ such that $f(x',y)\le K+\varepsilon$ for every $y\in v$.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ continuous and convex in the first variable on $X$ for each $y\in Y$
$f$ concave in the second variable on $Y$ for each $x\in X$
$f$ bounded above and below on $X\times Y$
replaced:
Let $X, Y \subseteq \bbr$ and $f : \bbr \to \bbr \to \bbr$ satisfy the convex-compact
minimax hypotheses, and suppose $f$ is normalized so that $0 \le f(x,y) \le 1$ for all
$x \in X$ and $y \in Y$. Fix an integer $M \ge 2$, a row sample
$x : \mathrm{Fin}\,M \to X$, a real $\varepsilon > 0$, and a finite column sample
$v \subseteq Y$. Write
\[
  K \;:=\; \sup_{y \in Y}\; \inf_{i \in \mathrm{Fin}\,M}\; f(x_i, y)
\]
for the indexed sampled lower value. Then the set
\[
  X \;\cap\; \bigcap_{y \in v} \bigl\{\, x' \in X : f(x', y) \le K + \varepsilon \,\bigr\}
\]
is nonempty; that is, there is a row $\bar{x} \in X$ with $f(\bar{x}, y) \le K + \varepsilon$
for every $y \in v$. This is the finite $\varepsilon$-net step in the proof of
Cesa-Bianchi--Lugosi Theorem~7.1.
